discussions.body: The Council was set to consider a proclamation declaring November 8, 2026, as Diwali, the Festival of Lights, celebrating the holiday's traditions, cultural significance, and message of compassion, harmony, and inclusiveness in the City of San José.

discussions.body: The Council was expected to adopt a proclamation declaring November 2026 as Alzheimer's Disease Awareness Month in honor of the 'Light the World in Teal' Global Alzheimer's Awareness Initiative to raise awareness and show support for those affected by Alzheimer's disease.

discussions.body: The City Manager and Council were scheduled to receive an update on labor negotiations during a closed session at 9:30 a.m., with the discussion continuing into the regular session at 1:30 p.m.

discussions.body: The Council was expected to accept the retirement plans' comprehensive annual investment fee reports for calendar year 2025, reviewing investment performance and fee structures.

discussions.body: The Council was scheduled to make multiple appointments to various boards and commissions, including retirement board public member interviews and deferred compensation advisory committee appointments.

discussions.body: The Council was set to approve a first amendment to the existing master consultant agreement with SCI Consulting Group on the consent calendar.

discussions.item: Receive a Joint Update on El Niño Preparedness for the 2026-2027 Rainy Season
discussions.body: The joint body was set to receive a comprehensive update on preparedness measures for El Niño weather patterns anticipated during the 2026-2027 rainy season. This briefing was expected to address readiness strategies and contingency planning for potential severe weather impacts affecting San Jose and the valley water district service area.

discussions.item: Receive an Update on the Anderson Dam Seismic Retrofit Project and Coyote Creek Flood Protection Project
discussions.body: The meeting was scheduled to include updates on two major infrastructure projects: the seismic retrofit work at Anderson Dam and ongoing flood protection improvements along Coyote Creek. These briefings were expected to cover project status, timelines, and progress toward enhancing public safety and infrastructure resilience.

discussions.item: Receive an Update on the Pure Water Silicon Valley Potable Reuse Project
discussions.body: The joint body was set to receive an update on the Pure Water Silicon Valley potable reuse initiative, which was expected to address the project's development, implementation status, and efforts to expand the region's water supply through advanced treatment and recycling technologies.

discussions.item: Amendment to Agreement with Santa Clara County for Criminal Justice Information System Access
discussions.body: The Council was scheduled to consider an amendment to the existing agreement between the County of Santa Clara and City of San José for access to the County's Criminal Justice Information Control System and Integrated Justice System. This consent item was set for routine approval.

discussions.item: Actions Related to Intent to Annex Territory to Community Facilities District No. 8
discussions.body: The Council was set to consider actions related to the annexation of territory to Community Facilities District No. 8. This item was expected to be approved as a consent calendar matter.

discussions.item: Regulation of Personal Delivery Devices in City Right-of-Way
discussions.body: The Council was scheduled to consider actions related to regulating personal delivery devices operating in the city's right-of-way. This item was set for consideration as part of the Transportation & Aviation Services section of the agenda.

discussions.item: Affordable Housing Development at 1510 North 1st Street
discussions.body: The Council was set to consider actions related to an affordable housing development project located at 1510 North 1st Street. This item was expected to be approved as a consent calendar matter under Community & Economic Development.

discussions.item: Arena Hotel Redevelopment and Homekey Program Transition
discussions.body: The Council was scheduled to consider actions related to the Arena Hotel Redevelopment project and its transition under the Homekey Program. This consent item was set for routine approval under Community & Economic Development matters.

discussions.item: Master Consultant Agreements for Citywide Sanitary and Storm Sewer Flow Monitoring
discussions.body: The Council was set to consider master consultant agreements with ADS Corp. and V&A Consulting Engineers for citywide sanitary and storm sewer flow monitoring services. This item was expected to be approved as a consent calendar matter.

discussions.item: Civil Service Commission Interview
discussions.body: The Council was scheduled to conduct a Civil Service Commission interview, with this item set to be heard last during the meeting. This item was expected to take place following all other agenda items.

THE LEVINE ACT

The Levine Act requires a Party in a Proceeding before the City of San José that involves any action related to their contract, license, permit, or use entitlement to disclose any campaign contributions to City elected or appointed officials totaling more than $500 within the 12 months prior to the City decision. A Participant to a Proceeding may voluntarily report a campaign contribution. For more information: https://www.sanjoseca.gov/your-government/appointees/city-clerk/levine-act

How to provide spoken Public Comment:

1) By Phone: (888) 475 4499. Webinar ID is 982 2147 4336. Alternative phone numbers are: US: +1 (213) 338 8477 or +1 (408) 638 0968 or (877) 853 5257 (Toll Free) a. When prompted to enter your Participant ID, please dial the pound symbol (#); If you would like to raise or lower your hand at any time, please dial * 9. You may dial * 6 to mute/unmute. 2) Online at: https://sanjoseca.zoom.us/j/98221474336 a. Use a current, up to date browser: Chrome 30+, Firefox 27+, Microsoft Edge 12+, Safari 7+. Certain functionality may be disabled in older browsers including Internet Explorer. Mute all other audio before speaking. Using multiple devices can cause audio feedback. b. Enter an email address and name. The name will be visible online and will be used to notify you that it is your turn to speak. c. When the Mayor calls for the item on which you wish to speak, click on “raise hand.” When we reach your name, the City Clerk will give you permission to speak and a pop up will appear on your screen letting you know it is your turn. d. When called, please limit your remarks to the time limit allotted. 3) In Person:

Fill out a Speaker’s Card and submit it to boxes at the bottom of the Chambers. Do this before the meeting or before the item is heard. This will ensure that the name on the card is called for the item(s) that you wish to address, and it will help ensure the meeting runs smoothly for all participants by calling speakers in an orderly manner. You may remain anonymous, but please fill out a card so we may call you. You can put “anonymous speaker” or “no name” on the card. When the Council reaches your item on the agenda, the Mayor will open the public hearing and call your name. Please address the Council from the podium, which is located to the left of the City Clerk’s table. To assist you in tracking your speaking time, there is a display on the podium and on the screen above you. On the podium, the green light turns on when you begin speaking; the yellow light turns on when you have 30 seconds left; and the red light turns on when your speaking time is up.
How to submit written Public Comment before the City Council Meeting

Members of the public are encouraged to submit written comments to the City Council via eComment on the legistar calendar page (the eComment is the column on the far right). Click "eComment," and it will take you to the eComment page to leave comments via an easy webform. Alternatively, you may still email at city.clerk@sanjoseca.gov. Those emails will be attached to the Council Item under “Letters from the Public.” Please identify the Agenda Item Number in the subject line of your email. eComments post immediately to the website. For emailed comments, submit them no earlier than 10 days before the meeting and no later than 5:00 p.m. on the day before the meeting. Comments received after 5:00 p.m. on the day before the meeting may still be posted before the meeting, depending on the volume of submissions received. You may speak to the City Council about any discussion item that is on the agenda and under Open Forum for City Business that is not on the agenda.

A lifelong San José resident, Paz was a celebrated local sports legend at Lincoln High School and San José City College, even honored as San José Mercury News’ Athlete of the Year in 1967. Paz dedicated nearly four decades as an educator teaching business, leading the cheer program, and coaching basketball at Yerba Buena High School from its opening in 1971 to his retirement in 2010.
